reply:
**Claim RBv1-CLM-06_r2: Status: Settlement prepared for human approval**

The claims system shows the settlement staged as pending approval. A Veridia claims handler still needs to approve the €1,200 payment before anything is paid.

**Facts recorded**
- Policy VER-1004, holder Thomas Petit, Volkswagen Golf (2020), market value €15,500, licensed since 1 November 2008.
- Incident 8 October 2026; reported 10 October 2026 (2 days after the incident).
- Mr. Petit states he rear-ended the car in front in a traffic jam and that the fault is his. Mr. Blanc is named and signed the accident report with him.
- Repair quote: €1,500 for Mr. Petit's own car.
- Documents provided: damage_photos.zip, repair_quote.pdf, accident_report_signed.pdf. These were counted as provided but not opened.
- No exclusion signal found in the story: he was driving his own car, and nothing suggests alcohol, licence issues, racing or intent.

**Reasoning**
- **Coverage:** Damage to his own car after a collision is C2 collision damage, which is in the Policy Schedule. <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="1" name="Veridia contract"/>
- **Fault:** Being at fault does not block C2. The not-at-fault deductible waiver in Article 5.2 does not apply, so the standard deductible applies. <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="2"/>
- **Deductible:** The standard C2 deductible is €300. Article 5.3 (young-driver surcharge) does not apply, because he has held his licence for well over 3 years. <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="1-2"/>
- **Assessor:** Not required. Article 6.1 requires an independent assessor only when the repair cost is above €1,500, and the quote is exactly €1,500. <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="2"/>
- **Timeliness:** Reported 2 days after the incident, so the claims system marked it on time. Late claims are referred to a handler under Article 7.1; this one is not late. <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="3"/>
- **Exclusions and coverage:** No possible exclusion was flagged (Article 7.2), and C2 is in the schedule (Article 7.3). <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="3"/>
- **Documents:** All documents referenced in the email are in the claim file, so no request for documents is needed. Article 4 allows missing documents to be requested rather than refused, but none are missing here. <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="2"/>

**Amounts (from compute_settlement only)**
- Deductible: €300
- Payout: €1,200 (repair cost €1,500 minus €300 deductible, capped at market value). <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="2"/>
- Assessor required: No
- Payment is made within 15 days after a Veridia claims handler approves the compensation. <cite document_id="2630#10414" pages="2"/>

**Note on the process:** The claims sub-agent could not open the contract, so its first pass relied only on the policy schedule and the system checks. I checked the contract myself and the conclusions above hold. The 5-day reporting deadline (Article 4.1) was confirmed by the claims system, not by my own reading of Article 4.1.

**Claim log**
1. get_policy for VER-1004: returned the policy details and coverages C1 and C2.
2. create_claim: open, C2 in schedule, reported on time, documents present, no exclusion, no blocking issues.
3. compute_settlement: deductible €300, payout €1,200, no assessor.
4. stage_settlement: status pending_approval, €1,200.

**Draft message to the customer**

> Dear Mr. Petit,
>
> Thank you for reporting the accident of 8 October 2026 under policy VER-1004 (claim reference RBv1-CLM-06_r2). We have received your damage photos, repair quote and signed accident report. Your claim is now with a claims handler, who will confirm the next steps. We will contact you once that review is complete.
>
> Kind regards,
> Veridia Claims Team
